text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Delegates at the ongoing main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) annual convention in Lilongwe on Monday rejected proposals to merge into one party with another opposition Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) and instead resolved to shelve the move.

- Delegates to the ongoing MCP annual convention in Lilongwe were on Monday bewildered when they learned former president Kamuzu Banda's retirement speech had also rejected a proposed merger with another opposition Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) but the paragraphs had been deliberately skipped when read out.

- The controversial proposal to merge two opposition parties, Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) into one party has been shelved until further notice by the latter's annual convention in Lilongwe.

- Parliamentarians who won by-elections this year will be sworn in when the house meets next week although some of the results are being contested in courts, Deputy Clerk of Parliament Fahad Assani said on Monday.
